title: Express wishes, feelings and necessity
lessons:
## Goal: explain what matters to you
Express a wish, an emotion, a necessity or a doubt while preserving the difference between a fact and your attitude toward it. Understand others' reactions and write a reasoned request. The subjunctive is a useful mood in everyday language, not a decorative tense to insert into every sentence with que.

## Prerequisites and quick check
You need present ils and nous forms, infinitives, object pronouns, participles and the main time relationships from Chapters 10–14. Retrieve `ils prennent` — they take, `nous prenons` — we take, and `j'ai reçu` — I received. You will use both stems and compound forms. Start with a small usable set: `Il faut que je parte.` — I need to leave; `Je veux que tu viennes.` — I want you to come. Understand their meaning before expanding the forms.

## 1. Build the present subjunctive
For many verbs, take the present ils form, remove -ent, and add -e, -es, -e, -ions, -iez, -ent. From ils parlent, make `que je parle, que tu parles, qu'elle parle, que nous parlions, que vous parliez, qu'ils parlent` — that I/you/she/we/you/they speak, with meaning supplied by the main clause. Regular -er singular forms often sound just like the indicative, so an audible change is not required. From ils finissent, make `que je finisse` — that I finish. From ils prennent, make `que je prenne` — that I take. For verbs with two stems, nous/vous normally use the present nous stem: `que nous prenions, que vous preniez` — that we/you take; `que je vienne`, but `que nous venions` — that I come, that we come. Similarly: `que je boive`, `que nous buvions` — that I/we drink.

High-frequency irregulars deserve full retrieval. Être: `que je sois, que tu sois, qu'il soit, que nous soyons, que vous soyez, qu'elles soient`. Avoir: `que j'aie, que tu aies, qu'elle ait, que nous ayons, que vous ayez, qu'ils aient`. Faire: `que je fasse`, `que nous fassions`; aller: `que j'aille`, `que nous allions`; pouvoir: `que je puisse`, `que nous puissions`; savoir: `que je sache`, `que nous sachions`; vouloir: `que je veuille`, `que nous voulions`. These mean that I/we be, have, do, go, can, know, want; the whole clause supplies natural English. `Il faut` becomes `qu'il faille`, but the frequent useful frame is il faut que plus another verb. Do not try to derive sois from the regular pattern.

## 2. Match the mood to the message
After a wish about another subject: `Je souhaite que vous réussissiez.` — I hope/wish that you succeed. After necessity: `Il faut que nous trouvions une solution.` — We need to find a solution. After emotion: `Je suis contente que tu sois là.` — I am happy you are here. After doubt: `Je doute qu'il comprenne.` — I doubt that he understands. Emotion can refer to an actual fact; subjunctive does not mean false. Here the main clause frames your reaction rather than simply asserting the fact.

When the same person controls both actions, an infinitive is often simpler: `Je veux partir.` — I want to leave. Compare `Je veux que tu partes.` — I want you to leave. `Je suis heureux de vous voir.` — I am happy to see you, versus `Je suis heureux que vous soyez ici.` — I am happy you are here. Avoid je veux que je parte for a straightforward same-subject intention.

Affirmative belief/knowledge commonly takes indicative: `Je pense qu'il est prêt.` — I think he is ready. `Je sais qu'elle vient.` — I know she is coming. Negated belief commonly takes subjunctive: `Je ne pense pas qu'il soit prêt.` — I do not think he is ready. Questions can vary with how doubt is presented; use a secure model rather than a claim that every question forces one mood. Affirmative espérer normally takes indicative, often future for a future hope: `J'espère qu'elle viendra.` — I hope she will come. Compare `Je souhaite qu'elle vienne.` — I wish her to come. Do not choose mood by translating hope alone.

## 3. Useful conjunctions and their contrasts
Use subjunctive after pour que, avant que, bien que, à condition que, and jusqu'à ce que: `Je répète pour que tu comprennes.` — I repeat so that you understand. `Appelle avant que le bureau ferme.` — Call before the office closes. `Bien qu'il pleuve, nous sortons.` — Although it is raining, we are going out. `Je resterai jusqu'à ce que tu reviennes.` — I will stay until you return. The present subjunctive can refer to future time; French has no ordinary future subjunctive for this task. With the same subject, prefer pour/avant de plus infinitive: `Je relis avant de signer.` — I reread before signing.

By contrast, après que takes indicative in standard French: `Après qu'il a signé, nous avons payé.` — After he signed, we paid. Parce que normally takes indicative for an asserted cause: `Je pars parce que je suis fatigué.` — I am leaving because I am tired. A formal ne can appear after avant que or fear expressions without being negative: `avant qu'il ne parte` — before he leaves. Recognize this optional ne explétif; do not add pas unless you mean actual negation. `Je veux qu'il ne parte pas.` — I want him not to leave, is genuinely negative.

## 4. Past subjunctive: an action already completed
Use present subjunctive avoir or être plus a participle: `Je suis ravie que vous ayez trouvé une solution.` — I am delighted that you have found a solution. `Je regrette qu'elle soit partie.` — I regret that she has left. The action is complete relative to the reaction or reference point. Compare `Je souhaite qu'il termine.` — I want him to finish, with `Je suis contente qu'il ait terminé.` — I am happy he has finished. Agreement rules remain familiar: `Je suis heureuse qu'elles soient arrivées.` — I am happy they arrived. `Les lettres qu'il ait écrites` can occur in a suitable subjunctive context, with preceding-object agreement; do not force a complex relative into ordinary speech. Pronominal contrast: `qu'elle se soit préparée` — that she has got ready, but `qu'elle se soit lavé les mains` — that she has washed her hands. Negation surrounds the auxiliary: `Je regrette que vous n'ayez pas reçu le message.` — I regret that you did not receive the message.

## 5. Sound, register and English traps
Listen to `il vient / qu'il vienne`, `il prend / qu'il prenne`, `il est / qu'il soit`. The stem or final consonant can make mood audible. In `qu'ils aient`, the subject ending does not sound like a full extra syllable. Avoid adding an English should inside every subjunctive clause: il faut que tu viennes already expresses the necessity. A polite request can be `Pourriez-vous venir ?` — Could you come? without subjunctive; grammar should serve the relationship. Browser voices are synthetic and cannot supply all natural conversational cues. Retry failed audio; do not count reading the script as successful listening.

## 6. Attempt before reveal
A. Express a wish that a colleague can attend. B. State your belief that she is available, then your doubt. C. React happily to two women's completed arrival. D. Say you reread so you can understand, keeping one subject.

:::answer
A. `Je souhaite qu'elle puisse venir.` — I hope she can come. B. `Je pense qu'elle est disponible. Je ne pense pas qu'elle soit disponible.` — I think she is available. I do not think she is available. C. `Je suis content qu'elles soient arrivées.` — I am happy they have arrived, said by a male speaker; contente for a female speaker. D. `Je relis pour comprendre.` — I reread in order to understand. A different subject uses pour que: `Je relis pour que tu comprennes.` — I reread so that you understand.
:::

## 7. Four skills, review and remediation
Listen for the desired action and the feeling behind it. Read for what is known versus wished; do not infer that subjunctive facts are untrue. Speak from a new situation and request action respectfully. Write an organized message with a reason, a wish and a practical next step, not a trigger-phrase checklist. Reuse Chapter 14 advice and earlier-past explanations. Work through bank groups of 25 in separate sessions. An adjustable four-hour split is 35 minutes recall, 45 listening, 40 reading, 45 speaking, 45 writing and 30 error review. Revisit in one day, three days, seven days and two weeks. Log the whole trigger-plus-clause, not an isolated conjugation. If mood choice fails, sort fact, wish, necessity and emotion examples; if formation fails, retrieve eight frequent irregular chunks. Self-rubrics support reflection, not examiner-equivalent or NCLC grading.

bank.en: We want everyone to take part.

bank.prompt: Negate the main clause and adjust the subordinate verb to express doubt.

bank.en: I doubt she knows this rule.

bank.fr: Il n'est pas certain que le bureau ouvre lundi.

bank.fr: J'espère que vous avez reçu mon message.

activities.title: A constructive concern
activities.prompt: What does the speaker want the organizer to do?
activities.script: Je suis contente que l'atelier ait attiré autant de monde. Pourtant, je crains que les débutants n'osent pas poser leurs questions. Il faut que nous gardions un moment pour eux à la fin. Je souhaite aussi que les consignes soient affichées, pour que chacun puisse les relire. Je ne demande pas d'annuler les exercices avancés.
options: Reserve question time and display instructions.
Reduce attendance to the original group.
activities.explanation: The speaker welcomes attendance but wants beginner access: dedicated question time and written instructions. Advanced exercises are explicitly not to be cancelled.

activities.title: Relief after a problem
activities.script: Je suis soulagé que vous ayez retrouvé le dossier. Hier, je pensais qu'il était perdu. Maintenant, je voudrais que vous vérifiiez les signatures avant de l'envoyer. Il faut aussi que nous fassions une copie. J'espère que le destinataire nous répondra cette semaine.
options: The signatures have all been checked.
activities.explanation: Ayez retrouvé presents finding the file as completed. Checking, copying and receiving a reply are still desired or expected actions.

activities.title: Known fact versus desired change
activities.prompt: Which statement is asserted as a known fact?
activities.passage: Je sais que la salle est petite. Je souhaite pourtant que tout le monde puisse participer. Il serait utile que nous proposions deux séances plutôt qu'une seule. Je ne pense pas qu'une simple réduction de la durée suffise. J'espère que le centre acceptera cette solution.
options: The centre has accepted two sessions.
A shorter session will certainly solve the problem.
activities.explanation: Je sais que asserts the room's small size. Participation and two sessions are wishes/proposals, and acceptance is a hope.

activities.title: A deadline with a purpose
activities.passage: Merci de vérifier vos coordonnées avant que nous imprimions les cartes. Il faut que toute correction soit envoyée avant jeudi midi. Après que nous aurons reçu vos réponses, nous lancerons l'impression. Nous souhaitons que chacun ait sa carte à l'ouverture du centre lundi.
options: Print first and correct details on Monday.
Wait until opening day to send corrections.
Send corrections before Thursday noon so printing can follow.
Collect cards before submitting any details.
activities.explanation: Corrections are due before Thursday noon. Receipt of responses precedes printing; the aim is for everyone to have a card at Monday's opening. Après que uses indicative futur antérieur here.

activities.title: A request that respects others
activities.prompt: You are helping organize an invented group activity. Explain one known fact, one concern, one wish about another person's action, and one necessity. React to a completed helpful action. Halfway through, imagine someone says: We cannot add more staff. Adapt your request without blaming anyone.
activities.model: Je sais que notre équipe est petite et je suis contente que les bénévoles aient préparé la salle. Je crains toutefois que les nouveaux participants ne comprennent pas les consignes. Je souhaite que nous affichions une version courte à l'entrée. Il faut aussi que quelqu'un réponde aux questions. Nous ne pouvons pas ajouter de personnel ? D'accord. Alors, je propose que nous regroupions les questions au début de chaque séance. Cela permettrait aux bénévoles de se concentrer ensuite sur l'activité. J'espère que cette organisation conviendra au groupe.
rubric: Fulfillment: fact, concern, wish, necessity and reaction to completed help.
Interaction: adapts to the staffing limit.
Coherence: proposed change responds to the concern.
Range/control: mood and infinitive choices reflect meaning; common irregulars are usable.
Intelligibility/register: respectful, clear, and spontaneously phrased.

activities.title: Request an inclusive change
activities.prompt: Write 110–150 words to a course organizer. Invent an access or communication problem. Acknowledge a completed helpful action, state a fact and an emotion, request two practical changes and explain their purpose. Use subjunctive where useful, not in every clause.
activities.model:
Bonjour Madame,
Je suis contente que votre équipe ait envoyé le nouveau programme. Les dates sont maintenant très claires. Je sais cependant que plusieurs participants travaillent le soir et je crains qu'ils ne puissent pas assister à toutes les séances. Je souhaite que vous proposiez un résumé écrit après chaque rencontre, pour que chacun puisse suivre les étapes du projet. Il serait aussi utile que les documents soient disponibles avant le cours. Nous pourrions ainsi préparer nos questions et profiter davantage du temps ensemble. Je ne demande pas que les horaires changent immédiatement, mais il faut que les absents sachent comment rattraper les informations essentielles. Merci d'examiner ces deux propositions.
Cordialement,
Nora
rubric: Fulfillment: acknowledges help, states problem, requests two changes and gives purpose.
Organization: separates facts, feelings and proposed actions.
Range: uses appropriate wish, emotion and necessity frames.
Control: indicative/subjunctive contrast, irregular forms and past completion are clear.
Register: constructive request, not accusation; follows learning word guidance.
